tooltips.enhancedVad: Uses a more accurate energy-based Voice Activity Detector. Combines RMS energy analysis with WebRTC fallback for reliable speech detection. Recommended to keep enabled for production use.
tooltips.useProviderVad: Delegate VAD to the AI provider (e.g., Google Live, OpenAI Realtime) instead of running it locally. Enable this only if your provider supports server-side VAD and you want to offload processing.
tooltips.minUtterance: Minimum duration of speech (in milliseconds) before it is considered a valid utterance. Shorter values make the system more responsive but may pick up noise. Default: 600ms.
tooltips.maxUtterance: Maximum allowed duration (in milliseconds) for a single utterance. After this limit, the utterance is force-closed and sent for processing. Prevents stuck recordings. Default: 10000ms.
tooltips.utterancePadding: Extra silence (in milliseconds) added after speech ends before the utterance is finalized. Helps capture trailing words. Increase if words are being cut off. Default: 200ms.
tooltips.fallbackEnabled: Enable WebRTC-based VAD as a fallback when enhanced VAD is insufficient. WebRTC VAD is fast but less accurate. Recommended to keep enabled as a safety net.
tooltips.aggressiveness: WebRTC VAD aggressiveness level (0–3). 0 = least aggressive (more false positives, fewer missed speech). 3 = most aggressive (fewer false positives, more missed speech). Default: 1.
tooltips.startFrames: Number of consecutive speech frames required before WebRTC VAD considers speech started. Higher values reduce false triggers but add latency. Default: 3.
tooltips.endSilenceFrames: Number of consecutive silence frames required before WebRTC VAD considers speech ended. Higher values prevent premature cutoffs but add post-speech delay. Default: 50.
tooltips.upstreamSquelch: Suppress non-speech audio frames before sending them to the AI provider. Useful for providers with server-side VAD (like Google Live) to reduce bandwidth and prevent false triggers from background noise.
tooltips.baseRms: Minimum RMS energy level for a frame to be considered speech. Frames below this threshold are squelched. Increase in noisy environments, decrease in quiet ones. Default: 200.
tooltips.noiseFactor: Multiplier applied to the adaptive noise floor. A frame must exceed (noise_floor × factor) to pass. Higher values = stricter filtering, may miss quiet speech. Default: 2.5.
tooltips.noiseEmaAlpha: Exponential Moving Average alpha for noise floor estimation. Lower values make the noise floor adapt slower (more stable). Higher values adapt faster to changing noise. Range: 0.0–1.0. Default: 0.06.
tooltips.minSpeechFrames: Minimum consecutive speech frames before squelch allows audio through. Prevents single-frame noise spikes from passing. Default: 2.
tooltips.squelchEndSilence: Number of consecutive silence frames before squelch stops forwarding audio. Acts as a mini hold-open timer. Default: 15.

tooltips.chunkSize: Size of each audio chunk sent to the AI provider (in milliseconds). Smaller chunks = lower latency, more network overhead. Larger chunks = more efficient, but higher latency. Default: 20ms.
tooltips.sampleRate: Audio sample rate in Hz. Must match your Asterisk configuration. 8000 Hz is standard for telephony (G.711). Do not change unless your system uses wideband (16000 Hz).
tooltips.jitterBuffer: Jitter buffer size (in milliseconds) to smooth out network timing variations. Larger buffer = more resilient to jitter but adds playback delay. Default: 950ms.
tooltips.connectionTimeout: Maximum time (in milliseconds) to wait for a provider connection before giving up. Increase if your AI provider has slow cold starts. Default: 120000ms (2 minutes).
tooltips.keepaliveInterval: Interval (in milliseconds) between WebSocket keepalive pings to the AI provider. Keeps the connection alive through firewalls/NATs. Default: 5000ms.
tooltips.providerGrace: Grace period (in milliseconds) after sending audio before expecting a provider response. Prevents premature timeout errors during initial provider processing. Default: 200ms.
tooltips.continuousStream: When enabled, audio is streamed continuously to the provider even during silence. Required for providers like Google Live and OpenAI Realtime. Disable only for chunk-based STT providers.
tooltips.diagEnableTaps: Enable diagnostic audio taps. Records raw audio streams (upstream and downstream) to disk for debugging. WARNING: generates large files. Use only for troubleshooting.
tooltips.diagOutDir: Directory where diagnostic audio tap files are saved. Must be writable by the AI Engine container. Default: /tmp/ai-engine-taps.

tooltips.defaultPrompts: Default system prompts sent to the LLM at the start of every conversation. These are applied globally unless a Context overrides them. Use 'system' role for behavioral instructions, 'user' for example inputs, 'assistant' for example responses.
tooltips.promptRole: The role of this prompt message. 'system' = instructions for the AI, 'user' = simulated user input, 'assistant' = simulated AI response. Most setups use a single 'system' prompt.
tooltips.promptContent: The actual text of the prompt message. For system prompts, describe the AI's personality, rules, and behavior. Keep it focused and concise for faster processing.

tooltips.format: Audio encoding format for the AudioSocket stream. 'slin' (Signed Linear 8kHz PCM) is the standard for Asterisk. 'ulaw' (μ-law) is an alternative Asterisk codec. Must match your Asterisk channel codec.
tooltips.host: IP address or hostname the AudioSocket server listens on. Use '127.0.0.1' for local connections (same machine as Asterisk). Use '0.0.0.0' to accept connections from remote Asterisk servers.
tooltips.port: TCP port for the AudioSocket server. Must not conflict with other services. Default: 8090. Ensure this port is open in your firewall if Asterisk is on a different machine.

bargeIn.title: Barge-in Settings
bargeIn.desc: Configure how callers can interrupt the AI agent during responses.
bargeIn.controlDesc: Allow callers to interrupt the AI while it's speaking.
bargeIn.enableDesc: Allow users to interrupt the AI agent during TTS playback.
bargeIn.enableTooltip: When enabled, the engine immediately flushes/stops local agent audio when it detects caller speech during an agent response.
bargeIn.energyThresholdTooltip: Caller energy threshold (RMS over PCM16) for provider-owned mode. Higher = less sensitive (fewer false barge-ins), lower = more sensitive (better for quiet callers). For pipelines, see 'Pipeline Energy Threshold' in Advanced settings below.
bargeIn.minDurationTooltip: Minimum sustained caller speech time required before triggering barge-in. Higher reduces false triggers but feels less responsive.
bargeIn.cooldownTooltip: Minimum time between barge-in triggers. Prevents repeated triggers from echo/noise after an interruption.
bargeIn.postTTSTooltip: Guard window after agent audio ends. Helps avoid self-echo or tail audio being mistaken as caller speech.
bargeIn.outputSuppressTooltip: After a barge-in, locally suppress provider audio briefly so previously generated speech doesn’t “resume” mid-sentence.
bargeIn.tuningTip1: Increase if barge-in is too sensitive (500-1200 typical)
bargeIn.tuningTip2: Increase if provider resumes speaking pre-barge audio (800-1600ms typical)
bargeIn.tuningTip3: Increase if you see immediate re-triggers after TTS ends (200-600ms typical)
bargeIn.advancedDesc: Additional knobs for provider-owned vs pipeline modes.
bargeIn.initProtectTooltip: Short guard window at the start of agent output to avoid triggering on initial burst/codec artifacts.
bargeIn.greetProtectTooltip: Extra guard window during the initial greeting turn (useful if greetings are short and prone to false triggers).
bargeIn.providerFallbackDesc: Use local VAD fallback only for providers that don’t emit explicit interruption events.
bargeIn.providerFallbackTooltip: If enabled, the engine can trigger barge-in using local VAD only after media is confirmed and only for the providers listed below.
bargeIn.providerFallbackProvidersTooltip: Comma-separated provider names where local fallback may apply (e.g., google_live, deepgram).
bargeIn.suppressExtendTooltip: While caller keeps speaking after a barge-in, extend suppression so agent doesn’t resume too early.
bargeIn.chunkExtendTooltip: While suppressed, extend suppression when provider chunks keep arriving (prevents tail audio from restarting output).
bargeIn.talkDetectDesc: Use Asterisk TALK_DETECT for robust barge-in during local file playback.
bargeIn.talkDetectTooltip: Recommended for local_hybrid: Asterisk DSP detects caller speech even during ARI file playback.
bargeIn.pipelineMinTooltip: Pipeline-specific minimum speech duration (more sensitive than provider-owned mode).
bargeIn.pipelineEnergyTooltip: Pipeline-specific energy threshold (more sensitive than provider-owned mode).
bargeIn.talkDetectSilenceTooltip: Asterisk TALK_DETECT(set) silence threshold in ms. Higher treats more audio as ‘silence’.
bargeIn.talkDetectTalkingTooltip: Asterisk TALK_DETECT(set) talking threshold (DSP energy). Higher requires louder speech to trigger.
bargeIn.restartWarning: Changes to barge-in configurations require an AI Engine restart to take effect.
bargeIn.restartSuccess: AI Engine restarted! Changes are now active.
bargeIn.forceRestartDesc: Do you want to force restart anyway? This may disconnect active calls.
bargeIn.restartedDegradedWarn: AI Engine restarted but may not be fully healthy

streaming.title: Streaming Settings
streaming.desc: Fine-tune real-time audio streaming performance and latency.
streaming.restartWarning: Changes to streaming configurations require an AI Engine restart to take effect.
streaming.restartSuccess: AI Engine restarted! Changes are now active.
streaming.playbackModeDesc: Choose how AI responses are delivered to callers.
streaming.downstreamModeTooltip: Use 'stream' for production (low latency). Use 'file' for debugging playback issues.
streaming.audioStreamParamsDesc: Core settings for audio packet handling.
streaming.jitterBufferTooltip: Buffer to smooth out network variations.
streaming.connTimeoutTooltip: Maximum time to wait for provider connection before failing (default: 120000ms = 2 min).
streaming.keepaliveTooltip: How often to send keepalive pings to prevent connection timeout (default: 5000ms).
streaming.graceTooltip: Wait time for provider response before considering it unresponsive (default: 200ms).
streaming.fallbackTooltip: Time before switching to fallback provider if primary fails (default: 8000ms).
streaming.lowWatermarkTooltip: Minimum audio buffered before playback starts - lower = faster but may be choppy (default: 80ms).
streaming.minStartTooltip: Minimum audio required before starting response playback (default: 120ms).
streaming.greetMinStartTooltip: Reduced min start for greetings - faster initial response (default: 40ms).
streaming.greetRtpWaitTooltip: ExternalMedia only: How long to wait for RTP endpoint before falling back to file playback for greeting (default: 250ms). Increase if greetings are cut off.
streaming.emptyBackoffTooltip: Max retries when buffer is empty before pausing playback (default: 5).
streaming.contStreamDesc: Keep the stream open even during silence.
streaming.normDesc: Normalize audio levels for consistent volume.
streaming.maxGainTooltip: Maximum volume boost applied to quiet audio (default: 18dB).
streaming.targetRmsTooltip: Target audio level for normalization - higher = louder output (default: 1400).
streaming.egressDesc: Control audio byte ordering and format for downstream playback.
streaming.egressSwapTooltip: Controls PCM16 byte ordering for downstream playback. 'auto' detects system endianness. Use 'swap' if audio sounds garbled/static, 'none' if already correct.
streaming.forceMulawDesc: Always encode egress audio as μ-law regardless of profile.
streaming.forceMulawTooltip: Force μ-law (G.711) encoding for all downstream audio. Enable if Asterisk expects μ-law but provider sends PCM16. Typically needed for telephony compatibility.
streaming.diagDesc: Tools for debugging audio stream issues.
streaming.enableTapsDesc: Record raw audio streams to disk for analysis.
streaming.outDirTooltip: Directory to save diagnostic audio recordings.
streaming.preSecsTooltip: Seconds of audio to capture before an event (default: 1).
streaming.postSecsTooltip: Seconds of audio to capture after an event (default: 1).

transport.hotReloadSaved: Configuration saved. Changes can be applied via hot-reload.
transport.restartSaved: Transport configuration saved. Restart AI Engine to apply changes.
transport.hotReloadAppliedPartiallyDesc: Restart AI Engine to fully apply changes
transport.hotReloadSuccess: AI Engine hot reloaded! Changes are now active.

transport.restartSuccess: AI Engine restarted! Changes are now active.
transport.bannerHotReload: Changes saved. Apply Changes to hot reload AI Engine without a restart.
transport.bannerRestart: Changes to transport configurations require an AI Engine restart to take effect.
transport.stasisAppTooltip: Name of the Stasis application in your dialplan. Must match the app name in your Asterisk configuration.
transport.transMethodDesc: Choose 'AudioSocket' for standard deployments or 'External Media' for RTP-based integration.
transport.bindHostTooltip: IP address the AudioSocket server listens on. Use 0.0.0.0 to listen on all interfaces.
transport.advHostTooltip: IP address Asterisk connects to. For NAT/VPN deployments, set this to your routable IP (VPN IP, public IP, or LAN IP). Leave as Bind Host for same-host deployments.
transport.rtpBindHostTooltip: IP address the RTP server listens on. Use 0.0.0.0 to listen on all interfaces.
transport.rtpAdvHostTooltip: IP address Asterisk sends RTP to. For NAT/VPN deployments, set this to your routable IP (VPN IP, public IP, or LAN IP). Leave as Bind Host for same-host deployments.
transport.rtpPortTooltip: Base UDP port for RTP streams (default: 18080).
transport.portRangeTooltip: Range of UDP ports for concurrent calls (format: start:end, e.g., 18080:18099).
transport.allowedHostsTooltip: IP addresses allowed to send RTP packets. Required when ASTERISK_HOST is a hostname. Comma-separated for multiple IPs.
transport.internalFormatDesc: Engine internal format. Pipelines typically expect 16kHz PCM16 (slin16).
transport.sampleRateHzTooltip: Auto-inferred from format if not set.
transport.extExpertDesc: Expose RTP source endpoint hardening controls.
transport.extExpertWarn: Warning: incorrect settings can drop RTP packets or break media connectivity.
transport.extExpertReadOnly: Expert values are visible and read-only until enabled.
transport.lockRemoteDesc: Drop RTP packets if source host/port changes mid-call.
transport.lockRemoteHardening: Security hardening: keep enabled unless your network path legitimately rewrites RTP source mid-call.

vad.title: Voice Activity Detection
vad.desc: Configure how the system detects speech and silence.
vad.restartWarning: Changes to VAD configurations require an AI Engine restart to take effect.
vad.forceRestartDesc: Do you want to force restart anyway? This may disconnect active calls.
vad.restartedDegradedWarn: AI Engine restarted but may not be fully healthy
vad.restartSuccess: AI Engine restarted! Changes are now active.
vad.primaryDetectDesc: Main VAD settings for speech detection.
vad.enhVadDesc: Use advanced algorithms for better accuracy.
vad.enhVadTooltip: Enables engine-side VAD (energy + optional WebRTC VAD) used for local heuristics like barge-in fallback and silence robustness. Does not change provider-owned turn-taking.
vad.useProvVadDesc: Prefer provider-managed turn detection when supported; engine VAD is used only for local fallback heuristics.
vad.useProvVadTooltip: When enabled, the engine avoids making primary turn/endpointing decisions and relies on provider-side detection where available. Engine VAD may still be used for safe local fallbacks.
vad.energyThreshTooltip: Engine VAD energy threshold (RMS over PCM16). Higher = less sensitive (fewer false triggers), lower = more sensitive (better for quiet callers). Only applies when Enhanced VAD is enabled.
vad.confThreshTooltip: Confidence required for engine VAD decisions (0.0–1.0). Used by engine heuristics; providers may implement their own confidence/endpointing. Only applies when Enhanced VAD is enabled.
vad.adaptThreshDesc: Adapt energy threshold based on observed noise floor.
vad.adaptThreshTooltip: When enabled, engine VAD raises the effective energy threshold in noisy environments so background noise doesn’t trigger speech.
vad.noiseAdaptRateTooltip: How quickly the adaptive threshold reacts to background noise (0.0–1.0). Higher reacts faster but can over-adjust on short noise bursts.
vad.engineVadDesc: Engine-side fallback heuristics (barge-in + safety), using WebRTC VAD when available.
vad.enableEngineFallbackDesc: Allow periodic forwarding / heuristics during extended silence (engine-side).
vad.enableEngineFallbackTooltip: If the engine believes the caller is silent for too long, it periodically lets audio through to avoid getting “stuck” on mis-detected silence. Does not affect providers that continuously stream audio.
vad.fallbackIntervalTooltip: After this much detected silence, engine may periodically allow audio through for robustness (default: 1500ms). Increase to reduce background noise leakage; decrease if calls feel “stuck”.
vad.aggressivenessTooltip: WebRTC VAD aggressiveness (0–3). Higher = more aggressive silence detection (fewer false speech triggers) but may miss quiet speech.
vad.startFramesTooltip: Number of consecutive “speech” frames needed to declare speech started. Higher reduces false starts but increases detection latency.
vad.endSilFramesTooltip: Number of consecutive “silence” frames needed to declare speech ended. Higher avoids cutting off trailing words but increases tail latency.
vad.utteranceDesc: Fine-grained utterance boundary tuning for engine-side heuristics.
vad.uttExpertDesc: Enable editing of low-level utterance timing and buffer controls.
vad.uttExpertWarn: Warning: these controls can clip speech, delay turn-taking, or over-buffer audio if tuned aggressively.
vad.uttExpertReadOnly: Expert values are visible and read-only until enabled.
vad.minUttDurationTooltip: Minimum duration to consider detected speech a valid utterance.
vad.maxUttDurationTooltip: Hard cap for a single utterance before forced boundary handling.
vad.uttPadTooltip: Extra audio kept around utterance boundaries for naturalness.
vad.fallbackBufTooltip: Internal fallback buffer size used by engine-side VAD fallback paths.
vad.upstreamSquelchDesc: Optional upstream noise squelch for continuous-audio providers with server-side VAD.
vad.enableUpsqDesc: Replace non-speech frames with silence for server-VAD providers.
vad.enableUpsqTooltip: When enabled, the AI Engine analyzes inbound PCM16 energy and replaces low-energy/noise frames with silence before forwarding audio to providers that require continuous audio and have native VAD. This can improve end-of-turn detection in noisy environments, but overly aggressive settings can clip quiet speech.
vad.baseRmsTooltip: Minimum RMS threshold in PCM16 space. Higher blocks more low-energy audio (less noise leakage) but may suppress quiet callers.
vad.noiseFactorTooltip: Dynamic threshold multiplier: threshold = max(base_rms, noise_floor_rms × noise_factor). Increase to be more conservative about what counts as speech.
vad.noiseEmaAlphaTooltip: Noise floor smoothing factor (0–1). Higher adapts faster to changing background noise but can overreact to short bursts.
vad.minSpeechFramesTooltip: Hysteresis: number of consecutive speech frames required before the engine considers the caller “speaking”. Higher reduces false positives but can increase detection latency.
vad.upsqEndSilFramesTooltip: Hysteresis: number of consecutive silence frames required to exit speaking state. Higher avoids toggling during noise, but may keep speech ‘open’ longer.
